summary.title: Application Resilience Engineering & Operations at Netflix
summary.one_liner: Learn the resilience patterns Netflix used in production (bulkheads, circuit breakers, fallbacks) and why operating them is as hard as coding them.
takeaways: Distributed applications have latent failures and drift, so each application must handle latency and failure in its own relationships rather than relying on infrastructure alone.
Common resilience patterns include bulkhead isolation (threads and semaphores), circuit breakers, fail fast, fail silent, and several fallback types (static, stubbed, network cache).
Implementing resilience patterns in code is only half the work; deploying, configuring, operating and maintaining them is a separate body of knowledge.
Operating resilient systems means finding weaknesses and managing drift as components change over time.
summary.summary: This is a slide deck from Netflix's talk at Velocity 2013 on building resilient distributed applications. It argues that systems drift from resilience and that applications must tolerate latency and failure in their dependencies themselves. It lists the resilience patterns Netflix used in production, including bulkheads, circuit breakers, fail fast/silent, and several fallback styles. The page text is brief, so it gives the pattern names and core thesis rather than implementation detail.
